questions.topic: What Development Promises — Different People, Different Goals
questions.stem: A student comparing two countries finds that average income is the single figure usually quoted for each of them, and asks a teacher why that one number cannot settle which country fares better. Consider the following statements. 1. A comparison of the two countries by average income alone will not show that in one of them most citizens are poor and one person is extremely rich, while in the other people are neither very rich nor extremely poor. 2. Average income is useful for comparison but it does not tell us how this income is distributed among people. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.stem: For a school project on how states differ, a student gathers the per capita income of Haryana, Kerala and Bihar and wants to know both which of the three stands highest and what the per capita income numbers actually stand for. Consider the following statements. 1. Of the three, Haryana has the highest per capita income. 2. The per capita income numbers for these states are of Per Capita Net State Domestic Product at Current Prices for 2023–24, and can be taken roughly as the per capita income of the state. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.stem: A student is asked in class what people actually hope development will give them, and finds that the answer is much wider than money. Consider the following statements. 1. People think not only of better income but also have goals such as security, respect for others, equal treatment and freedom in mind. 2. Besides average income, a nation or a region has no other attributes that can be thought of as equally important. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.
